correctness.rationale: The proof starts from the exact circumradius/ball-segment identity, expands an exact cross-section factorization uniformly for all half-distances in the unit ball, evaluates the beta integrals exactly, and uses the published exact half-distance moment formula. The remainder remains uniformly integrable. Symbolic and numerical consistency checks reproduce the planar coefficient, the three-dimensional coefficients, and fourth-order residual scaling. The extreme-value correction follows from the logarithm of the exact maximum distribution, with the ordinary binomial correction separately retained in dimension three.

value.rationale: The coefficient resolves the first term hidden in the lead theorem's relative second-order remainder for every fixed dimension and turns the qualitative Fréchet limit into an explicit first convergence correction. In dimensions at least four that geometric term is the dominant finite-sample correction, while in dimension three it combines nontrivially with the binomial correction to give the exact coefficient \(1147/182\). The invariant is natural, dimension-uniform, and directly attached to a newly established exact tail law rather than to an arbitrary parameter slice.
